figures.side: Right lateral sinus, as identified by the source caption
figures.authorReportedAbnormality: Interruption of the proximal right lateral sinus on MIP reconstructions and a lateral-sinus filling defect on source-slice images suggesting thrombus.
figures.visibleAnnotations: Four original lowercase panel labels a, b, c and d; no added arrows.
figures.patientLinkage: The caption presents the four panels as one imaging example but gives no explicit patient identity or acquisition registration. Do not claim temporal comparison or registration.
figures.scope: The delivered composite contains rendered MIPs and two static source-slice screenshots. It supplies no native volume, measured flow, exact occlusion length or thrombus segmentation.
figures.exactCaption: CE-MRV. From left to right: (a,b) maximum intensity projection (MIP) reconstructions; interruption of the proximal portion of the right lateral sinus; (c,d) native slices; defect in the lateral sinus suggests a thrombus.

figures.side: Superior sagittal sinus at the midline
figures.authorReportedAbnormality: Spontaneous hyperdensity in the superior sagittal sinus on nonenhanced CT, and peripheral enhancement surrounding a central filling defect on enhanced CT (empty delta sign).
figures.visibleAnnotations: Two original lowercase panel labels a and b; no source arrow.
figures.patientLinkage: The source pairs the panels as a demonstration of CT signs, without explicitly stating patient identity, scan interval or image registration.
figures.scope: The caption calls panel b enhanced CT. Use that acquisition description rather than adding a named CTV protocol. These single selected sections do not establish full thrombus extent.
figures.exactCaption: CT. From left to right: (a) nonenhanced CT: spontaneous hyperdensity of the superior sagittal sinus, (b) enhanced CT: empty delta sign testifying to the circulation of contrast around the thrombus, which appears as a defect of signal in the center of the superior sagittal sinus.

figures.side: Deep veins in panel A; left caudate head and thalamus in panel B, as identified by the source caption
figures.authorReportedAbnormality: Deep cerebral venous thrombosis with absent flow in the internal cerebral veins and vein of Galen, associated with hemorrhagic transformation of a venous infarct in the left caudate head and thalamus.
visiblePanels: MR venogram with one orange arrow
figures.visibleAnnotations: Original uppercase labels A and B and orange arrow in A. The arrow is identified by the source as the internal cerebral veins.
figures.patientLinkage: The figure caption explicitly describes a 27-year-old woman with deep CVT and assigns both panels to that clinical example. It gives no registration or timing claim.
figures.scope: The source caption explicitly states that the straight sinus is not demonstrated. Neither a straight-sinus panel nor a complete venous study can be inferred.
figures.exactCaption: A 27-year-old woman with deep CVT. A: MR venogram showing a lack of flow in the internal cerebral veins (arrow), vein of Galen, and straight sinus (not demonstrated). B: Axial susceptibility-weighted MRI scan showing hemorrhagic transformation of a venous infarct in the left head of the caudate nucleus and thalamus.

reviewScope: Complete original images inspected visually against the original figure-specific captions and permissions. Clinical identifications remain author-reported. No native volume, segmentation or patient registration is supplied.
